text: You think Russia is bigger than Pluto? Most books agreed with you. Until 2015.
Russia is huge. 17.1 million square kilometers. 11 time zones.
And Pluto? Through Hubble? Just a blurry dot. About 2,300 kilometers wide.
Do the maths? Pluto's whole surface? About 16.6 million.
Russia wins. Then in 2006 it got worse for Pluto. Astronomers voted it out of the
Planet Club. Demoted and smaller than a country. So how do you measure a world
nobody has seen up close? You go there. NASA's new horizons flew for nine and a
years, nearly 5 billion kilometers. July 2015, it finally measured Pluto. 2377
kilometers wide. Bigger than the gas, so its surface? About 17.7 million. Pluto beats
It's Russia! By about 650,000 square kilometers. Almost a whole Texas. Russia still has 11
time zones though. Small comfort. Russia never shrank. We just finally looked. And the twist?
half of Pluto's famous heart has a Russian name, Sputnik Planitia, named after Earth's
first satellite launched by the Soviet Union. So on paper, a little piece of Pluto is still
Russian. So, who's bigger now? This is Bughal. Follow for more geography fun facts.
